title: From Signal Processing to Digital Control

contract.reader: An engineer or student who has the discrete-time tools of the DSP series and basic feedback vocabulary, and has to implement or analyze a controller on a computer
contract.problem: What changes when a feedback loop is closed through an ADC, a computer and a DAC, and how to choose the discretization method and the sampling rate
contract.outcome: Derive the zero-order-hold equivalent of a first-order plant; compute the stability limit sampling imposes on a proportional loop; choose between forward Euler, backward Euler and Tustin; implement a digital PI with clamping; estimate the phase cost of the hold and of computation delay; choose a sampling rate from a phase budget
contract.contribution: One first-order plant, shared with the continuous-time control series, analyzed exactly in discrete time, with two scripts showing the sampling-induced oscillation and the windup effect, and a sampling-rate rule derived from one formula
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; two NumPy scripts with their real output; Astrom and Murray (2008), Astrom and Wittenmark (1997), Franklin, Powell and Workman (1998), Oppenheim and Schafer (2010)
contract.limitations: First-order plant only in detail; no direct discrete-time design beyond a pointer to pole placement; nonlinear effects other than saturation not treated

findings.problem: ZOH equivalent, stability bound (coth), integral update and phase-lag formula cut at the right edge with no scroll cue; each result is restated nearby
findings.whyItMatters: Readers meet an incomplete formula where it is derived
findings.action: Break the ZOH equivalent and the stability bound after the first '=', the phase-lag chain into two lines; shorten or break the integral update
findings.acceptance: On new 360 px captures none of the four displays is cut

findings.location: Section 1.1 flowchart and Section 1.2 sequence diagram
